goal: Let a brand find the conversations worth joining. Given a set of topics, poll each connected platform's public search on a cadence, dedupe the results into a reviewable queue that never shows the same post twice, and hand a person the permalinks to engage with themselves. The engaging stays manual on every platform and that is a finding, not a timidity: Meta has no like/react API at all (Facebook's was deprecated in Graph v6.0, Instagram's IG Media object has no likes edge, Threads has never had one), and Bluesky — which does expose app.bsky.feed.like — names 'generating automated or bulk interactions, including any that would cause a notification to a user like a message, follow, like or reply' as its own definition of spam. Docket therefore automates discovery, which is where the hours actually go, and automates nothing that touches another person's notifications. Both verdicts are recorded with sources in docs/research/meta-discovery.md and docs/research/bluesky-discovery.md so neither is re-litigated.
prerequisite: 077-engagement-inbox (PR #121) must merge to main first. That entry builds the seams this roadmap consumes rather than reinvents: polling inside runTick() with a per-account cursor and lease, the provider capability seam for a read-side platform feature, the insert-only ledger in the shape of external_item_claims, the immutable stored copy of what a third party wrote, and the docs/privacy.md amendment covering third-party personal data stored without that person's involvement. Starting entry 1 before #121 lands would mean either duplicating those seams or rebasing onto a moving foundation. As of 2026-10-16 that PR is OPEN and MERGEABLE but BEHIND main, with another session actively pushing to it.

entries.title: A topic discovery queue, Bluesky first
entries.description: Today Docket has no read side for other people's content except what 077-engagement-inbox ingests about the brand's own posts. A brand owner who wants to engage with a topic — 'Halloween decorations' for Stencilvania — searches the platform by hand, scrolls, judges relevance, and has no memory of what they already saw last week. Automate the finding. Add two tables via a committed migration (`pnpm db:generate`, `pnpm db:check` green): `discovery_topics` (projectId, a display name, the query string, the target accountId whose credentials and platform the search runs under, an enabled flag, a poll cadence, and `lastPolledAt`/`nextPollAt`/lease columns claimed exactly as 077 claims per-account polling work and as src/server/services/standing-series claims due series) and `discovered_posts` (projectId, topicId that first surfaced it, platform, the platform's own stable id, permalink, author handle where the platform provides one, the post text as returned, postedAt, discoveredAt, and a review state of new / dismissed / engaged). Dedupe is a database constraint, not application logic: unique on (projectId, platform, externalId) so a post found by two topics appears once, following the ledger shape in src/server/db/schema/external-claims.ts — insert-only, and the stored copy of what somebody wrote is immutable for the same reason 077 makes inbound items immutable. Poll from a new `discovery` section in src/server/scheduler/index.ts alongside the seven that already run there, with its own time budget, heartbeat and counts, claiming due topics under a lease so overlapping ticks and mid-run kills cannot double-insert or lose a cursor; it must respect the same rule 077 establishes, that publishing wins the per-account budget and discovery spends only what is left. Add a read-side `discovery` capability to the provider contract in src/providers/types.ts following the capability seam 077 introduces, implemented for Bluesky only — every other provider declares it unsupported and the UI says so rather than offering a dead control. Bluesky search is `app.bsky.feed.searchPosts` with `q`, `tag`, `since`/`until`, `lang`, `limit` (max 100) and `cursor`; the one concrete code gap is in src/providers/bluesky/client.ts, whose `agentFor` builds a plain Agent with only an authorization header — `@atproto/api` sets the `atproto-proxy` header only when `withProxy()`/`configureProxy()` has been called, so a searchPosts call as written today would hit the brand's own PDS, which does not implement an AppView-only lexicon. The search agent must be built with `.withProxy("bsky_appview", "did:web:api.bsky.app")`, and a test must prove the header is present, because the failure mode without it is a confusing 404 from the user's own PDS rather than an obvious misconfiguration. Each result's `viewer.like` tells Docket whether the brand account already engaged, so an already-liked post can be marked rather than re-offered. Retention is part of this entry, not a follow-up: discovered posts are other people's personal data stored without their involvement, so they purge on a bounded schedule through the existing housekeeping section (src/server/scheduler/housekeeping.ts) and the docs/privacy.md language 077 adds must be extended to cover discovered posts explicitly — this is a reviewable queue, not an archive. UI: a Discover screen under src/app/p/[projectSlug]/ listing topics (create, enable, pause, delete; owner/admin for writes, enforced server-side via src/server/auth/access.ts) and the queue of new posts since the reviewer last looked, each row carrying the permalink as the primary action, with mark-engaged and dismiss recorded against the member who did it; follow the docket-ui skill and docs/design-system.md, announce outcomes through a LiveRegion, label every control, full keyboard use, and real empty states for 'no topics yet' and 'nothing new'. Tests: migration, the dedupe constraint under concurrent inserts, lease-based claiming across overlapping ticks and a mid-run kill, the proxied-agent header, cursor paging, retention purge, project isolation, authz for editor vs admin, and tests/integration/security/secret-scan.test.ts. Record in docs/decisions.md why liking is not automated, citing both research docs. This entry does NOT add Threads or Instagram discovery (their own entries, each gated on an App Review that only the deployer can file), does NOT add any automated like, follow, repost or reply on any platform, does NOT add a relevance classifier or spam filter — 077 already decided Docket does not judge strangers' content on a brand's behalf, and the same logic holds here — and does NOT expose discovery over the v1 API or MCP, which belongs in a later entry once the data model has settled.
entries.rationale: First because it is the only entry that can ship without an external approval, and because every platform-agnostic part of the feature lives here: the topics model, the dedupe constraint, the scheduler section, the retention story and the review UI are perhaps eighty percent of the work and are identical whatever platform lights up next. Bluesky is the right first provider for exactly the reason 077 chose it — app-password auth already works, no app review stands in the way, and the credentials Docket holds already carry the scope a read needs — so the infrastructure gets proven end to end against a platform that cannot block it. Doing this first also means the Threads and Instagram entries reduce to a provider adapter plus an App Review submission, rather than carrying the whole feature's design with them.

entries.title: Threads keyword search as a second discovery provider
entries.description: Add Threads to the discovery capability built in `topic-discovery-queue`. Threads is the best-supported discovery surface of the three Meta platforms and the research says so plainly (docs/research/meta-discovery.md): `GET /keyword_search` has existed since December 2024, is explicitly designed to surface other users' public posts, returns a `username` per result — which Instagram's hashtag search does not — reaches back to Threads' 2023 launch rather than a rolling window, and carries a roomy budget of 2,200 queries per 24 hours per user with no-result queries free. Implement it as a `discovery` capability on the existing provider in src/providers/threads/, reusing the topics model, dedupe constraint, scheduler section, retention purge and Discover UI from entry 1 without modification — if this entry needs to change any of those, that is a signal the seam in entry 1 was drawn wrongly and should be fixed there rather than worked around here. Map the endpoint's results onto `discovered_posts` including the author username, which the UI should show because it is the field that lets a reviewer judge whether a thread is worth answering before opening it. Error mapping matters: a Standard Access token silently searches only the authenticated user's own posts rather than failing, so Docket must detect that it has not been granted Advanced Access and surface it as a clear 'Threads discovery needs App Review for threads_keyword_search' state on the Discover screen rather than quietly returning an empty or self-only queue that reads as 'no results'. Respect the per-user daily budget with a counter that stops polling before the cap rather than discovering the cap through an error, and record what happens when it is hit. Update docs/research/meta-discovery.md with anything the live integration contradicts, and docs/decisions.md with the access-level handling. **Prerequisite outside the pipeline:** this entry assumes `threads_keyword_search` Advanced Access has already been granted on the deployer's own Threads app. Filing and passing that App Review needs a Meta dashboard, a real app and a human, so it is explicitly NOT a task in this spec — the same reasoning that made 077's Meta identity spike a human task that starved its implement loop until it was moved last. Track the filing outside the roadmap and start this entry once access is granted. This entry does NOT add Instagram or Facebook discovery, does NOT add any engagement action, and does NOT change the topics model or the queue schema.
entries.rationale: Second rather than third because it is the cheaper and better-value Meta integration by a wide margin: the Threads provider and app credentials already exist in src/providers/threads/, the net-new engineering is a single read adapter, and the data it returns is strictly richer than Instagram's — an author username and real history instead of an anonymous rolling 24 hours. Its gate is also the lighter of the two, needing App Review for one permission rather than App Review plus Business Verification plus a separate Public Content Access feature. Putting it ahead of Instagram means the second provider proves the capability seam generalises while the heavier approval is still in flight.

entries.title: Instagram hashtag search, within its three hard limits
entries.description: Add Instagram to the discovery capability as the third provider, accepting that it is the narrowest of the three and designing around limits rather than discovering them in production. Per docs/research/meta-discovery.md: `GET /ig_hashtag_search` resolves a hashtag name to an id, then `GET /{id}/recent_media` or `/top_media` returns public media, under Facebook Login for Business — the login path Docket already uses — needing `instagram_basic` plus the 'Instagram Public Content Access' feature plus Advanced Access via App Review and Business Verification. Note also that the live documentation moved: the `developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-api/...` URLs that search engines still surface now 404, and the current reference lives under `instagram-platform/instagram-graph-api/reference/ig-hashtag*`. Three limits shape the implementation. First, **thirty unique hashtags per rolling seven days** per IG user — a cap on distinct topics, not on query volume, so polling the same thirty repeatedly is free but adding a thirty-first silently costs a slot for a week. Docket must track the distinct hashtags it has resolved in the trailing seven days and refuse to add or poll beyond the cap with a clear explanation, because the failure is invisible otherwise. Second, **`recent_media` reaches back only twenty-four hours**, which means the queue can only accumulate forward from the day a topic is created, no backfill is possible ever, and any day the scheduler does not run is lost permanently — so this provider needs at-least-daily polling, and the Discover screen must tell the reviewer plainly when a gap in coverage occurred rather than presenting an incomplete queue as complete. Third, **no author field exists at all** — the docs state you cannot request `username` on returned media objects — so the UI must present an Instagram row honestly as an anonymous permalink the reviewer has to open, and the author column that Threads populates stays empty rather than being faked from the caption. Adding the required permission and feature also changes Docket's Meta OAuth scope set in src/providers/meta/oauth.ts, which currently requests pages_show_list, pages_manage_posts, pages_read_engagement, instagram_basic and instagram_content_publish; widening it means every already-connected Meta account must be reconnected to grant the new access, so this entry owns that migration — detect accounts holding a pre-widening grant, surface a reconnect prompt through the existing connect-banner path (src/server/services/connect-banner.ts), and never let a silently under-scoped token present as an empty result set. Tests: the rolling-seven-day hashtag budget including the boundary, the twenty-four-hour window and coverage-gap reporting, the absent-author presentation, under-scoped-token detection and the reconnect prompt, plus project isolation, authz and the secret scan. **Prerequisite outside the pipeline:** Advanced Access with Business Verification and Instagram Public Content Access must already be granted on the deployer's own Meta app. That filing is a human task and explicitly NOT a task in this spec, for the same reason as the Threads entry. It is also the least certain of the three approvals — Meta may decline Public Content Access for a single-brand app — so this entry may never start, and nothing earlier in the roadmap depends on it. This entry does NOT add Facebook discovery, for which nothing buildable exists, and does NOT add any engagement action.
entries.rationale: Last because it is the most gated, the most limited, and the only entry that might be refused outright by a third party. Its approval is the heaviest of the three — App Review plus Business Verification plus a separate feature grant — and Meta may well decline Public Content Access for an app serving one brand, so no earlier entry may depend on it. It is also the entry whose value is most constrained by the platform itself: an anonymous permalink from a rolling twenty-four-hour window is genuinely less useful than a Threads result carrying a username and real history, which is why it follows rather than leads the Meta work despite Instagram being the brand's primary channel. Placing it last means its scope-widening migration, which forces every connected Meta account to reconnect, lands once against a queue and a UI that two providers have already exercised.
